topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the framework of cancer evolution, and presents the session's learning objectives.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution Driven by Genetic and Epigenetic Alterations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through Darwinian clonal selection powered by sequential genetic mutations and transient epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Role of Cell of Origin and Tissue Hierarchy in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cell of origin and position within tissue hierarchies influence susceptibility to malignant transformation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Promotion of Incipient and Established Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate that cancer outgrowth depends on permissive microenvironments and inflammatory signals in addition to genetic alterations.

topics.label: Experimental Technologies for Investigating Tumor Biology
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the experimental and computational technologies used to study tumor evolution and microenvironmental interactions in human tissue.

topics.label: Synthesis of the Multi-Factorial Evolutionary Model of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the lecture's themes into a unified evolutionary model where cancer progression requires the convergence of cell-intrinsic and microenvironmental conditions.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
